name: Timothy
overview: The Scriptures introduce Timothy as a young disciple from Lystra, uniquely born of a Jewish mother and a Greek father, whose faith was well regarded among the local believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul chose Timothy as a trusted companion, circumcising him to maintain Jewish customs for ministry effectiveness among Jewish audiences (Acts 16:3). Throughout their missionary journeys, Timothy remained a faithful partner, staying behind in Berea while Paul traveled, and later joining him in Corinth and Macedonia to assist in preaching the gospel and strengthening the early churches (Acts 17:14-15; 18:5). These passages highlight Timothy’s integral role in Paul’s ministry and his dedication to spreading the message that Jesus is the Christ.
